correctness.rationale: The full 123-face simplicial complex and all 22 local complexes are exhaustively constructed from the exact graph. Acyclic Hasse incidence sorts cover 23 complexes, 1465 face occurrences, 3644 incidences and 709 matched pairs. Critical vectors reduce to (one 0-cell,two 2-cells) globally, (one 0-cell,two 1-cells) for links at v=3,4, (one 0-cell) for deletions there, and single one- or two-sphere wedges as claimed for every other v. Explicit free-face elementary collapses further prove collapsibility for v=3,4. Cell-attachment dimension forces wedge homotopy, beyond mod-two Betti ranks. Two standalone original-data verifiers execute successfully; the second independently checks full mod-two boundaries and characteristic polynomial.

originality.rationale: Theorem 3.4 in Barmak arXiv:1007.0418v1 only implies suspension for the bipartite Herschel graph; Engström arXiv:math/0508148v1 only supplies general graph reduction methods. The full exact local homotopy classification is not entailed by either. Published graph databases give combinatorial and spectral, not homotopy data. Equivalent object and stronger coverage searches reveal no decisive overlap, while unindexed literature remains a named risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed independent computation or a database entry under a different graph alias may already contain the exact classification.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the minimum-edge 11-vertex non-Hamiltonian polyhedral benchmark, and the exact integral homotopy and all eleven single-vertex links/deletions form a motivated complete local topological invariant of that canonical object. The two exceptional degree-three vertices are detected topologically even though six other degree-three vertices have noncollapsible deletion complexes. This dichotomy is more informative than ranks or independence polynomial alone, and its finite exhaustive certificates are reusable. No general theorem about Hamiltonicity is asserted.
